item.text: I’ll treat every flagged item as an assumption exactly as written and audit internal entailment only—no repository or source lookup. I’ll start with L5b/R-0 and the roster/retraction, then check the proof chain for any independent failure.

No critical error found. The main conditional proof chain is coherent, but REV 2 still has three justification/ledger gaps. In particular, L5b does not quite provide the advertised exact normalization pin, and the two `[S]` flags are not purely statement-matching as written.

1. L5b does not unambiguously establish the normalization consumed by STEEP — justification gap

> “a discrete valuation on K(x)\* extending v with index e₁⋯e_{r−1}”

followed by:

> “as a DISCRETE valuation (value group ℤ; the index clause normalizes  
> v_r|_K = e₁⋯e_{r−1}·v), v_r is integer-valued”

There are two problems internal to the display:

- “Extending \(v\)” ordinarily suggests \(v_r|_K=v\), whereas the next sentence asserts \(v_r|_K=(e_1\cdots e_{r-1})v\). These can be reconciled by treating “extension” as extension of the valuation ring/equivalence class, but that convention is not part of the quoted statement.
- “Discrete valuation” does not, without an explicit normalization or codomain, automatically establish that this particular displayed value function has value group exactly \(\mathbb Z\). The document inserts “value group ℤ” as a parenthetical conclusion rather than displaying it as part of the source statement.

This matters at the load-bearing step:

> “u₀, u₁ ∈ ℤ … so μ ∈ ℤ: writing λ_S = μ = −h_S/e_S in lowest terms gives e_S = 1”

If the ordinates were in the alternative fractional normalization acknowledged immediately above, that inference would not follow. The intended scaled normalization is internally plausible—and the formula \(v_r=e_{r-1}H_{r-1}\) supports it—but the advertised “exact source statement displayed” does not itself state enough to close the normalization question. Thus V18 finding 7 is improved but not completely discharged.

2. `(R-0)` is internally usable, but its claimed derivation is underexplained — justification gap

The flag says:

> “t₀ | F ⇔ F̄ is a positive power of ψ̄_j … so f_{t₀} … is the product of the irreducible factors of g with ψ̄_j-power reduction.”

The displayed H0 derivation does establish that every irreducible factor belongs to exactly one \(g_j\). But passage from a per-irreducible divisibility criterion to “the largest-degree factor divisible by \(t_0\) is the product of all such factors” additionally uses compatibility of type divisibility with products/factor clusters. That closure property is not stated in the quoted order-zero equivalence or H0.

Logically, the proof survives because the full product assertion can be read as part of the `(R-0)` assumption. But then it is not merely a consequence “DERIVED here given the flag (via H0’s per-factor clause)” from the displayed equivalence alone.

Apart from that presentation issue, the intended consequence is consistent:

- H0 partitions the irreducible factors into the \(g_j\).
- Given the asserted product characterization, \(f_{t_0}=g_j\).
- Then L5’s degree formula gives
  \[
  \deg\psi_j\,\omega_1(g)=\deg f_{t_0}=\deg g_j
  =a_j\deg\psi_j,
  \]
  hence \(\omega_1(g)=a_j\).

So `(R-0)` is not false; its assumption boundary is simply wider than its “derived via H0” wording suggests.

3. The `[S]` versus `[M]` roster is not clean — justification gap, not a theorem error

The package defines `[S]` as requiring only:

> “locating and quoting an exact GMN statement whose content is the flag”

Yet `(R-1)` asserts:

> “the constructed φ_r has one-sided N_i(φ_r) of slope λ_i with R_i(φ_r) ∼ ψ_i at every i ≤ r−1, top multiplicity 1.”

That is substantive mathematical information about every constructed representative and is load-bearing in REP-IRR. It may ultimately follow immediately from GMN’s definition of “representative,” but until the exact statement is produced, classifying it as purely `[S]` assumes the very source match still owed. On the material displayed here, `(R-1)` is mathematically substantive.

`(R-0)` is mixed:

- The order-zero divisibility equivalence is plausibly definitional/statement-matching.
- The exhaustive product characterization of \(f_{t_0}\) is mathematical factorization content unless product compatibility is included explicitly in the matched GMN statement.

Therefore both `[S]` entries contain mathematical content as written. This does not invalidate Theorem A because they are openly assumed, but the roster’s binary classification understates their present proof burden.

4. The retraction/consumption accounting is not literally complete — justification gap

The conditionality display says:

> “the proof consumes ALL FIVE §2 flags, at these steps and no others … (R-0) in (2)surjective and (3).”

But the roster itself also says `(R-0)` is consumed in:

> “the track-node/active-node alignment in Definition 𝒯(g).”

That alignment is also used implicitly in Theorem A’s injectivity argument. At root divergence, descendants of a track child must be associated with the corresponding H0 cluster \(g_j\); identifying that semantic track cluster with \(f_{t_0}=g_j\) is precisely `(R-0)`.

Thus “in (2)surjective and (3), at these steps and no others” is too narrow. The global flag assumption still covers the proof, so this is a consumption-ledger defect, not a missing premise or false conclusion.

The assertion:

> “No V18 finding is disputed”

is fair. But the stronger implication that every finding is completely repaired is not: the L5b normalization remains incompletely pinned, and the new `(R-0)` consumption is itself undercounted.

Full proof audit

The following portions check out, conditional on the displayed floor, the five flags understood at their full asserted strength, and the interface:

- H0: the Hensel decomposition and per-factor root-cluster assignment are sound.
- REP-IRR: the degree-exhaustion argument correctly upgrades the OM-SAT factor to the whole representative, conditional on `(R-1)`.
- NODE: the factorization, degree bookkeeping, coprimality, and recursion are coherent conditional on `(R-2)` and `(GMN-COH)`.
- STEEP: once integer-valued ordinates are granted, the convex-hull argument correctly produces a length-one negative side and hence \(e_S=d(S)=1\). The signed-slope issue from V18 finding 8 is repaired.
- Theorem A: finiteness follows conditional on `(R-3)` and `(GMN-COH)`; injectivity, surjectivity, telescoping, and the semantic checksum then follow.
- Theorem B: the weighted injection argument is correct. Positive missing-leaf weights make a proper complement impossible.
- Theorems C–E: the leaf verdict, distinctness, coverage, product, and invariant-multiset conclusions follow from A, B, and `(I-1)`–`(I-3)`.
- The deliberate non-consumption claims remain correct: no O-3 no-missing clause, Krasner radii, D-16, rate theorem, or cross-family invariance is secretly used.

The document is therefore not unsound: its principal conclusions are explicitly conditional, and no quoted passage proves a demonstrably false theorem. It is not fully sound as a verification closure, because L5b’s exact normalization and the true mathematical scope/classification of the `[S]` flags remain unsettled, and the revised consumption ledger still understates `(R-0)`.

VERDICT: SOUND-WITH-GAPS
